source: hand-authored fixture for issue #308 — not shipped data
description: The arrangement in which the string a FINDING prints and the string its collapsed KEY renders are not the same string. Levoketoconazole files TWO self-named allergy rules — 'levo', carrying the note 'opioid reaction', which an allergy recorded as 'Levocetirizine' reaches only mid-word and nothing corroborates, and 'ketoconazole', carrying 'other reaction', which no recorded allergen here reaches at all. contraindicationFinding keys both on the SUBSTANCE (issue #146), so contraindicationClauses renders them as ONE joined clause 'opioid reaction — other reaction', while the ledger's sentence prints only the matched rule's own note, 'opioid reaction'. A CONDITION rule on 'respiratory depression' carries that same note; it is not self-named, so it is corroborated by construction, and an allergy rule and a condition rule sharing one note is the 'recorded either way' shape DrugReferenceInjector.contraindicationSections' own comment names. The record therefore states 'opioid reaction' as this chart's reading — and the finding beside it prints exactly those words. No entry carries ATC codes, so no class comparison can chip.
